caption:
OpenAI bought Orchestra Bio, a startup whose AI agents help drugmakers keep big development programs on schedule.
The team will join Rosalind, OpenAI's life sciences models and tools.
Terms were not disclosed.

slides.headline: OpenAI just bought a biotech startup to put *AI agents* inside drug development

slides.heading: Agents that keep drugs *on schedule*
paras: OpenAI said Tuesday it bought Orchestra Bio, a San Francisco startup founded in 2022. Terms were not disclosed.
Its AI agents track drug programs and work out which deadlines a setback, like a failed manufacturing batch, will hit.

slides.heading: Humans still *make the call*
paras: The agents gather information and compare possible fixes, but scientists and program leaders make the final decision.
Orchestra had raised about $20 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and 8VC.

slides.heading: Folded into *Rosalind*
paras: The team joins Rosalind, OpenAI's AI models and tools for biologists and chemists, used by drugmakers like Moderna and Novo Nordisk.

paras.t: Rival Anthropic bought biotech startup Coefficient Bio in April.

slides.hook: AI labs are moving straight into medicine. Follow to see who gets there first.
